Order No. 05/ dated: 10th June, 2025 I.A. No. 6121 of 2025
1.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and the learned A.P.P. for the State.

2. This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail during the pendency of this
appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offence under Section 376 (2)(n) of the Ipc and Section
6 of the Pocso Act and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years along with a fine of Rs.
20,000/- for the offence under Section 6 of the Pocso Act.
4.  It has been alleged that the victim was enticed by the appellant and subjected to rape.

5. Submission has been advanced by learned counsel for the appellant that there was a relationship between the appellant and the victim for the last four months and in support of his contention, he has referred to the material exhibit-M1 which is the CD of the CCTV Footage from which it appears that the victim was already in contact with the appellant and was not scared when she was going with the appellant.

It has further been submitted that in fact the victim did not have grievance against the appellant but subsequently one Kishore Yadav who had seen the appellant and the Anil Yadav vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132986351/

This fact has been supported by the victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr. P.C.
It has further been submitted that the appellant is in custody since 13.08.2020.
6. Mrs. Anuradha Sahay, learned APP has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
7. The age of the victim has been assessed as 13-17 years.
Admittedly, she was a minor and the evidence of the victim as well as the other witnesses reveal about the commission of rape committed upon her by the appellant.
8. In view of the above, we are not inclined to admit the appellant on bail and the prayer for bail of the appellant is hereby rejected at this stage.
